jobs.title: Research Director, Audience Insights, Content Insights
jobs.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

 About the Role, Mission or Department Overview 

 The Research Director, Content Insights will have a critical role informing the creation, iteration and measurement of video and video products at the New York Times. You will lead all video measurement research to inform our understanding of how video content performs across platforms, surfaces, and audience segments. You will oversee the end-to-end measurement of video effectiveness, from individual videos to longer-form recurring concepts, and translate data into relevant strategies that inform production, distribution, and editorial decisions. You will also work with product, design, and editorial teams to improve on-platform video experiences.

 You will report to the Managing Director, News Products on the Audience Insights Team and will collaborate with partners across the Newsroom. You understand how to blend market research and user research methods and practices into actionable insights for an entire mission.

 This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

 Responsibilities: 

• Develop audience research to support the creation and growth of video franchises and recurring shows. Drawing on research methods used by production studios and streaming networks, you'll conduct research that can inform greenlight decisions — including concept testing, pilot testing, audience appetite studies, and competitive landscape analysis.

• Partner with video leadership to evaluate whether a format, host, or editorial premise has the demand to sustain an audience over time. For existing shows, help build longitudinal tracking that monitors audience health: loyalty, satisfaction, and reasons for churn.

• Help build a video performance tracking program grounded in survey-based measurement, tracking metrics like awareness, recall, engagement, and sentiment among defined audience segments over time.

• Working alongside analytics teams, you'll help establish benchmarks, monitor performance across all surfaces where video is published (owned and operated, social, streaming), and develop a consistent cadence of reporting that gives editorial, product, and business stakeholders a reliable read on how our videos are landing with audiences.

• Lead quantitative and qualitative research among target audiences to support video strategy and format development (e.g., format preference studies, thumbnail and title concept tests, viewer satisfaction studies). Partner with video producers and editors to understand their needs and scope appropriate methodologies, from brief development through questionnaire design, survey launch, and insight delivery.

• Manage multiple research projects and ad-hoc requests simultaneously, developing timelines and planning resources.

• Partner or lead research on other editorial projects and franchises, such as newsletters, podcasts, or other emerging products

• Collaborate with research partners, analytics teams, and company partners.

• Identify opportunities to improve the quality, speed, and effect of video measurement, including recommending new vendors, tools, and methodologies.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

 Basic Qualifications: 

• 10+ years of experience in market research, user research, or consumer insights, with an emphasis on multimodal and product research.

• Proficiency in both qualitative and quantitative research methodologies and experience with continuous improvement and new ideas.

• Experience leading all facets of a tracking program, including vendor relationships, questionnaire development, data mining, and reporting.

• Fluency in analyzing large datasets, identifying insights, and creating clear reports.

• Experience developing timelines across multiple projects, applying project management skills.

• Experience managing external research partners/vendors.

• Experience with visualization tools and creating compelling presentations.

 Preferred Qualifications: 

• B.A./B.S. degree.

Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

jobs.description:
The big picture: Axios is a modern media company dedicated to providing trustworthy, award-winning news content in an audience-first format. We’re hiring a Head of Live Editorial to join our award-winning events team, Axios Live!

 Why it matters: Axios Live is one of Axios’ three core business pillars, bringing Axios journalism to in-person and virtual audiences through interviews, panels, roundtables, and executive forums. This senior editorial leader will oversee macro people management, connect the Booking and Coverage silos, and serve as the primary liaison between Axios Live and the broader newsroom. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Global Head of Axios Live, this role ensures our live events portfolio meets Axios’ editorial standards, reflects diverse perspectives, and strengthens Axios’ position at the forefront of news and business storytelling.

 Go deeper: This is a high-impact leadership role with broad editorial and operational responsibilities, including but not limited to:

 Axios Live Editorial Leadership 

• Set the editorial vision and strategy for Axios Live programming across all event formats.

• Ensure all Axios Live editorial outputs, including onstage interviews, marketing materials, recap articles, and post-event coverage, meet Axios’ editorial standards and Smart Brevity style.

• Exercise sound editorial judgment in fast-moving news environments, adapting programming as news develops and ensuring live-event scripts, materials, and coverage assets are ready for breaking-news needs.

• Lead and develop the Axios Live editorial team, including editors, bookers, coverage leads, and Managing Editor; oversee team structure, role design, performance management, and career development.

• Foster a collaborative, high-performing culture aligned with Axios’ mission and values.

• Serve as the primary liaison to the broader newsroom, aligning editorial priorities, event coverage, and resource sharing.

• Partner with Communications to align on timely promotion, amplification, and coverage of Axios Live events, while identifying opportunities to grow the Axios brand, audience, and event reach.

• Lead rigorous copy editing and final editorial review of Axios Live’s external-facing materials, including event scripts, moderator notes, speaker introductions, marketing copy, run-of-show materials, recap stories, social copy, and other audience-facing assets, to ensure accuracy, clarity, consistency, and adherence to Axios’ editorial standards and Smart Brevity style.

 Programming and Standards 

• Develop event concepts, programming arcs, and editorial frameworks for all Axios events, summits, and larger Axios-hosted programs.

• Shape a diverse, compelling Axios Live programming portfolio that keeps Axios at the forefront of news, policy, and industry storytelling.

• Partner with Sales and Partnerships to design sponsored and branded programming that maintains editorial integrity.

 Strategy and Innovation 

• Contribute to the strategic growth of Axios Live, including new formats, verticals, and revenue opportunities.

• Demonstrate comfort with and understanding of AI, automation, and emerging tools, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability, and quality across research, booking, production, and editorial workflows.

• Represent Axios Live internally and externally, and potentially onstage at live events, as a senior editorial voice.

 Connect Booking and Coverage 

• Own the connective tissue between Booking, including securing newsmakers and influencers, and Coverage, including event language, recaps, live-tweeting, and post-event content.

• Ensure seamless coordination among editorial, events, sales, and partnerships so programming is editorially sound and commercially compelling.

 Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit, a deep passion for Axios’ mission and journalism, and the following skills:

• 12 - 15+ years of journalism or editorial experience, including significant experience leading teams and complex editorial operations.

• Significant experience in live news, events, TV or video production, or related fields.

• Proven success working in, or closely with, a newsroom and building strong cross-functional relationships.

• Excellent writing, copy editing, and research skills, with exceptional attention to detail, keen news judgment, and storytelling ability.

• Deep familiarity with digital and social media landscapes and how news travels across platforms.

• Strong understanding of Axios’ Smart Brevity style and the ability to teach and uphold it across a team.

• Demonstrated ability to lead and scale editorial teams, including managers and senior individual contributors.

• Ability to operate in high-pressure situations, meet tight deadlines, and make calm, sound decisions under pressure.

• An extensive rolodex of senior leaders, policymakers, CEOs, and other newsmakers, along with the ability to scout, pitch, and book editorially sound guests for high-profile onstage moments.

• Understanding of how editorial excellence supports business goals, including sponsorships, partnerships, and ticketing.

• Ability to travel for major events and activations, which may include Davos, Cannes Lions, SXSW, CES, Climate Week, and political conventions.

• Experience with video editing, live production, or broadcast is a plus. A background in media, policy, Capitol Hill, or political campaigns is also a plus.

Because this is a remote-optional job posting, this salary range takes into account all possible locations within the United States, but candidates will only be eligible for the salary range for their location.

All team members are expected to actively develop AI literacy and use AI tools to enhance their productivity, creativity, and efficiency. jobs.title: Editorial Director, Brand & Creative Partnerships
jobs.location: US: SF, NYC, Seattle and Remote
jobs.description:
Who we are 

 About Stripe 

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

 About the team 

 Stripe’s Narrative & Editorial team brings together Content Marketing, Brand Marketing, Portfolio Product Marketing, Copywriting, Copy Editing, and Customer Marketing. We create coherent, distinctive stories about the businesses, technologies, and economic forces shaping the internet.

 What you’ll do 

 We are hiring a senior editorial leader to help bring original stories and insights from Stripe–based on our data, expertise, and customer conversations–to a broader audience via media partnerships and other brand marketing channels. This person will be an exceptional editor, writer, and creative partner with strong instincts about what earns attention: an argument worth making, an unexpected angle, an elegant execution, or a piece of work that people genuinely want to share.

 This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the leader of Stripe’s Narrative & Editorial team. The role will spend most of its time shaping major external media partnerships, with the remainder split between helping with original editorial work and advising partner teams on new ideas and their execution.

 Responsibilities 

• Lead the editorial and creative direction for Stripe’s most important external media partnerships, including advertising content, research-led collaborations, and original editorial programs developed with respected publishers and creators.

• Develop work that feels native to the audience and editorial environment in which it appears—not generic brand messaging placed beside someone else’s work.

• Turn Stripe’s original data analyses, economic insights, customer stories, and more into content pieces that are clear, surprising, useful, and memorable–and that readers and listeners won’t want to skip over.

• Shape the full editorial process for partnership work: refining briefs, identifying the strongest ideas, directing creative development, and providing decisive feedback on drafts and final deliverables.

• Direct and manage agencies, external creators, and editorial partners as needed, working within existing partnership structures and commercial agreements.

• Write, edit, and materially improve high-stakes content across formats, including blog posts, newsletter segments, podcast scripts, ad copy, social posts, and more.

• Generate original concepts for creative programs, editorial franchises, and nontraditional formats that broaden how Stripe contributes to conversations about the internet economy.

• Serve as a trusted thought partner to teams across Stripe, helping them clarify ideas, find the strongest expression of their work, and make better creative decisions.

• Partner with colleagues in Brand Marketing, Brand Design, Content Marketing, Portfolio PMM, Copywriting, and Customer Marketing to make Stripe’s storytelling more coherent and distinctive.

• Define and uphold a clear quality bar for editorial and partnership work, making well-reasoned calls about what is ready to represent Stripe and what still needs improvement.

 Who you are 

 We are looking for someone with exceptional editorial judgment and a demonstrated ability to make complicated ideas compelling. You may have developed that experience in a newsroom, independent publication, creative studio, agency, research institution, technology company, or another rigorous creative environment.

• You have 8+ years of relevant experience in editorial, writing, creative development, journalism, publishing, media, brand strategy, or a closely related field. This may include experience writing consistently for a large online followership, even if not professionally.

• You have an exceptional portfolio of published or public-facing work that demonstrates strong writing and editing, original thinking, and an ability to make ideas resonate with an audience.

• You are, in the best sense, very online: an active reader of and contributor to the newsletters, social platforms, and niche communities where people debate new ideas about technology, economics, science, business, and culture. You can spot emerging arguments, voices, and formats early—and engage with them authentically, with intellectual honesty and your own point of view.

• You are an excellent editor. You can diagnose what is missing from a draft or idea, identify the most interesting argument, and give feedback that makes the work materially better.

• You have experience developing original editorial work, sponsored media, advertising, creative partnerships, or other high-quality audience-facing programs.

• You understand the difference between work that is merely on-message and work that is genuinely interesting, useful, or worth discussing.

• You can translate complex subjects—including technology, business, economics, science, or policy—into work that is accessible without becoming simplistic.

• You have strong creative instincts and a sophisticated design sensibility. You understand how language, ideas, visuals, format, and distribution work together.

• You are deeply curious about the technology industry and the broader cultural and economic context in which it operates.

• You are comfortable influencing senior stakeholders, external partners, writers, designers, marketers, and agencies without relying on formal authority.

• You can move fluidly between strategy and execution: developing the core idea, shaping the brief, improving the draft, and making the final call on quality.

• You have high standards, sound judgment, and enough pragmatism to help teams make excellent work within real constraints.

jobs.description:
About Builders
 Builders is a non-partisan movement of millions, uniting Americans across lines of difference, grounded in the belief that curiosity, compassion, courage, and creativity can move us beyond division. Founded by Daniel Lubetzky, our community spans 5M+ citizens, 650M video views, and 400+ movement partners including José Andrés, Katie Couric, Adam Grant, Lonnie Ali, and Karl Rove. Through a growing ecosystem of content, tools, partnerships, and activations, we turn civic engagement into meaningful action, empowering people to participate, collaborate, and deliver real-world impact to enact lasting change.
 About the Position
 Builders is searching for a communications leader who is already operating in what comes next. This role leads traditional comms/PR and extends into all communication verticals, including CRM, SMS, social, and key campaign messaging. We are looking for a plugged-in leader in the news, politics, media, or lifestyle space who has mastered the fundamentals of earned media and brings deep, trusted relationships across the political media landscape on both sides of the aisle.
 Reporting to the Chief Marketing Officer, you will own Builders' communications and editorial strategy and lead its earned media operation, driving coverage across national and Texas outlets, independent media, creator, and emerging platforms.
 This is a communications-first role with editorial upside. The editorial scope gives the right leader room to shape how Builders thinks and speaks across channels and strengthen our audience strategy.
 Responsibilities
 Communications Strategy and Leadership

• Set and own Builders' communications strategy, aligning earned media, editorial, and organizational priorities with clear goals and measures of success.

• Serve as the judgment-setter on if, when, and how Builders engages in cultural, political, and civic conversations at the national and Texas levels.

• Lead crisis and rapid-response communications, aligning messaging across channels during key news cycles.

• Develop messaging and communications frameworks for dedicated campaigns and evergreen content, ensuring consistency, clarity, and cross-partisan credibility across all channels.

• Lead and develop communications and editorial team members and freelancers, setting a high bar for quality, speed, and voice.

• Own the communications tech stack and champion the thoughtful use of AI tools.

• Report on coverage, share of voice, and audience impact, using data to make strategic decisions, not just report metrics.

 Earned Media and Pitching

• Lead the proactive earned media operation, identifying story angles, shaping pitches, and securing coverage across national outlets and key regional markets, most notably Texas.

• Monitor the news and culture cycle in real time to spot reactive opportunities and move credibly and quickly.

• Treat creators as a core earned media channel, building relationships to reach audiences traditional press does not, in partnership with the Social team.

 Political and Media Relationships
 • Bring and expand a network of trust-based relationships with journalists, producers, and editors who cover politics, civic life, and solutions-oriented news, positioning Builders as a go-to source for cross-partisan civic stories. 
 Editorial Voice and Content

• Help define and operationalize the "Builders lens": balanced, solution-oriented, values-driven commentary that safeguards organizational reputation and public trust.

• Distill complex policy and political issues into compelling content with non-partisan framing that moves audiences beyond "us vs. them" thinking and surfaces common ground.

• Lead the editorial calendar for the Builders and Builders TX newsletters, blog, and SMS, and contribute to social channels, aligning earned media moments with owned content.

 Requirements

• 7-10 years of PR or communications experience, with the majority in earned media (pitching, placing, and managing press) and at least 2 years leading strategy or managing people.

• A proven pitching track record: you can point to placements you drove in national and major regional outlets, and you know what made them land.

You turn what our R&D experts and executives know into original, fact-checked journalism that reporters quote, analysts cite, and buyers trust. You are one person working with roughly 10 subject-matter experts and executives, and you don't have a team to hide behind. If you do this poorly, phData publishes content that is forgettable at best and wrong at worst, in a market where credibility is the whole game.
 About You
 Read this section like a mirror, not a checklist. Some of it is meant to make you nod. Some of it is meant to make you uncomfortable. Both reactions are useful, to you and to us.

• You've killed a story you loved because one source wouldn't confirm it. You didn't publish and hope.

• You've told a senior executive their idea wasn't original enough to run, and kept the relationship.

• Journalist first. You report, interview, verify, and edit like someone whose name is on the byline. You consider "good enough to publish" a failure of standards, not a deadline.

• Quiet ownership. Your best work goes out under an SME's or executive's name. You are fine with that, and you still defend its quality as if it were yours.

• Judgment over volume. You pick one flagship idea a quarter and say no to the rest. You don't measure yourself by how much you shipped.

• Translator. You can sit with an R&D lead who is explaining agent orchestration, ask the question that exposes the real insight, and then explain it to a reporter in two sentences.

• Relationship builder. You earn attention from reporters and analysts by being useful and accurate, not by pitching harder.

 Original content

• Coordinate briefings, prep SMEs and executives, gather client references, and track phData 's inclusion in analyst reports.

 Internal communications and advocacy

• Run the employee advocacy program: select participants, provide shareable content, and track engagement.

 Program operations

• Publish the editorial calendar and lead monthly performance reviews.

• Set and enforce editorial standards for sourcing, fact-checking, and legal compliance. Own the content workflow.

 How you'll be measured

• Leading indicators: ideas submitted per quarter, threshold share volume, turnaround time for published views, and on-time newsletter delivery.

Director of AI Content Systems, Marketing
 Remote (United States or Canada, minimum 4-hour overlap with US Eastern hours) | Marketing | Reports to: VP of Marketing
 The role
 You won't write most of our content, you'll design, build, and run the AI-powered system (think content engineering) that turns product, customer, and expert knowledge into content that drives organic pipeline.
 You're not a software engineer, but you think like one. You're as comfortable vibe coding and building agents as you are customizing WordPress, writing brand guidelines, or proofreading a white paper.
 This is the first hire on a new team at Time Doctor . We run it like an engineering team whose product is content: a clear spec, a repeatable production system, quality gates, and measured output. The team stays small and gets its leverage from AI, automation, freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts.
 Who we are
 Time Doctor is a workforce analytics platform that gives distributed teams the visibility they need to improve trust and performance. We serve remote, hybrid and outsourced organisations worldwide, with particular strength in BPO, healthcare and tech services. We are bootstrapped, profitable and fully remote, with team members across 30+ countries. We built a durable business on customer revenue rather than venture capital, and we are now focused on growing it.
 What you'll own

• Content strategy. Decide what we publish, for whom, and why, based on search demand, AI-search behavior, buyer questions, and revenue marketing priorities.

• The content production system. Design and run the AI workflows, agents, prompt libraries, briefs, and QA gates that produce content at scale. Treat it like a product: version it, measure it, and keep improving it.

• Expert input pipeline. Build repeatable ways to capture knowledge from product, customer success, sales, customers, and outside experts, and feed it into the system so our content says things competitors can't.

• Verbal and visual brand. Own voice, tone, and editorial standards, and encode them into the system so every asset meets them by default.

• SEO and AI search (GEO). Own strategy for organic search and visibility in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and others).

• The website. Own site architecture, content structure, conversion paths, and the website roadmap.

• Tooling and vendors. Choose and manage the AI tools, automation platforms, and outside partners the team runs on, within a budget.

 How you'll be measured
 You own three outcomes: organic leads, organic traffic, and AI + SEO search visibility. Because organic results lag, your first two quarters are weighted toward leading indicators that show the system is working.
 What you'll manage and who you'll work with
 You'll build and manage: content development, technical SEO/GEO implementation, and visual design. You'll do the work yourself when speed matters, and bring in agencies, contractors, or freelancers you select and direct against our brand guidelines when scale matters.
 Your inputs: positioning, messaging, and personas come from the VP of Marketing. You turn them into content at scale; you don't own positioning.
 Your team: Freelancers and contractors as needed, with a path to hire as the system proves out.
 Requirements
 Who you are

 Must have 

• 5+ years in B2B SaaS content, SEO, or growth marketing, including 1+ years leading a function or program. 

• You've built and run AI-powered content workflows in production. You can walk us through one end to end: inputs, tools, prompts, skills, QA gates, output volume, and results. 

• Hands-on with AI and automation tools (LLMs, agents, and automation platforms). 

• Comfortable tinkering with HTML and CSS. Can read Python and scripts. Comfortable with Claude Code or eager to learn it. 

• A track record of growing organic traffic and leads through SEO, with a working understanding of how AI search surfaces and cites content. 

• Strong editorial judgment. You know when an AI draft is off-brand, generic, or wrong, and you design the system to catch it. 

• Experience directing freelancers, agencies, and subject-matter experts to a quality bar. 

• You think in systems and metrics: throughput, cycle time, cost per asset, and outcomes. 

 Nice to have 

• Experience owning a B2B website roadmap and conversion optimization. 

• Background in time tracking, workforce analytics, HR tech, or remote-work software. 

 This role is not a fit if you want to be the primary writer, or if your strength is CMS or content platform architecture rather than marketing outcomes. 
 How we'll evaluate 
 A walkthrough of a content system you've built, and a short exercise designing a workflow for one of our content types. We won't ask for writing samples. 
 Why this role 

• You are the first hire on a new team, and you get to design the content system from the ground up.

About the Role

Ad Age recently described us as "if Omnicom was rebuilt on AI." Your job is to turn a line like that into an argument the market repeats back to us. The split is roughly 80% Darkroom , 20% Shadow.
 We are making a category bet on the forward-deployed marketer , the operator who sits inside a business and builds with AI rather than briefing the work out. We intend to make that a term of art through Darkroom : the article, the LinkedIn engine, the video, the webinars, the press. You own that campaign end to end.
 You'll report to our VP of Marketing, who sets direction and makes the calls. You'll help shape the thinking behind it: how content maps to the funnel, which channels carry which offers, and what actually turns attention into pipeline. Then you build the content that proves it.
 Our marketing operations manager owns the calendar, the publishing, and the deployment. You make the content that fills all of it, across LinkedIn, video, email, paid, and creator, and you brief our designer, video editor, and SEO specialist so one idea becomes a post, a video, an email, and an ad in the same week. This isn't a writing-only role.
 Alongside content, you own the creative half of the creator program: who we work with, what we ask them to make, and the call on whether we go wide with many creators or deep with a few. You source and negotiate the partnerships and write the briefs. Marketing Ops runs the admin behind it. Creator content is one of our two strongest lead sources today and the one with the most room left in it.
 This is a New York-based role operating in the EST Time Zone, hybrid out of our new NYC office, and all business is conducted 100% in English.
 What you'll do

• Brand Narrative: Define and defend what Darkroom and Shadow say. Own the positioning arguments, the category bet, and the point of view that shows up everywhere else.

• Funnel & Strategy: Work with the VP of Marketing on how content builds pipeline: which channels, which offers, which lead magnets, and what the content has to do at each stage. You help build the model, then you feed it.

• LinkedIn & Video: Build our LinkedIn engine across the company page and our executives' accounts, including video made for the feed it runs in. This is where our buyers spend their day and where we have the most ground to take.

• Creator Strategy & Briefs: Decide who we work with and what they make. Source creators, negotiate the partnerships, write the briefs, and set the strategy between a wide roster and a small group of anchor creators. Marketing Ops handles the CRM, deadlines, content collection and reporting.

• Email & Newsletter: Own what goes into our newsletter and to our list. Marketing Ops handles deployment. The thinking, the cadence, and the reason anyone opens it are yours.

• Shadow Content: Take Shadow's content from scattered to a funnel: posts into webinars and lead magnets into signups. Product marketing for a platform that sells to operators.

• Paid Copy: Partner with our designer, video editor and performance team on the words behind our ads, so the organic and creator assets that work become the ads that work.

• Editorial Direction: Brief the team, review the work, and hold a consistent standard across every surface both brands touch.

• Events & Moments: Turn our NYC office, our activations, and our press into content programs instead of one-off posts.

• Measurement: Work with Marketing Ops on the weekly scoreboard: reach, follower growth, earned media value, and how content traffic converts.

 You should apply if this sounds like you

• You have owned content that was accountable to a business number. You can explain how a post becomes traffic, becomes a conversion, becomes a lead, and you have been graded at the end of that chain. If content has always been someone else's funnel, this role is not for you.

• You know this world. DTC, e-commerce, performance marketing, social commerce, AI tooling. You can write about TikTok Shop, retention, or attribution without a briefing and without getting it wrong.

• You have sourced, negotiated with, and briefed creators yourself. You know what separates a brief that produces something usable from one that wastes everybody's month.

• You have a public track record. A newsletter, bylines, a brand account you grew, a campaign that landed, a term you helped popularize. Send the link.

• You get output out of people who don't report to you, and you can give a designer or an editor feedback that makes the next version better.

• You already work with Claude, ChatGPT, or similar daily and have shipped real work with them. We are a Claude-first company.

 Hard disqualifiers

• No published writing or no portfolio link.

• Never sourced or briefed a creator yourself.

• Content experience with no accountability for pipeline.
